newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - DMG becomes market-maker in UK stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - DMG becomes market-maker in UK stocks.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) on Tuesday started market-making in UK stocks, marking another stage in the development of the investment bank's equity business in London.

Despite the troubles of DMG's fund management business, shaken by the high-profile departure of top fund manager Nicola Horlick, its securities business continues to progress towards its goal of offering an integrated pan-European equity service.

John Smith, head of UK equities at DMG -- a unit of Germany's Deutsche Bank -- told Reuters he had been "pleasantly surprised" by the level of business which the house had carried out on its first day of quoting prices in UK shares.
The launch was not officially announced but the firm had flagged its ambition several months ago. It brings the number of firms making markets in UK equities in London to 31.
"Across the board we have conducted a significant share of business and in certain stocks we have seen a very substantial share of business," Smith said.
He said DMG's eight UK equity market-makers had been quoting buy-and-sell prices in all 100 stocks in the blue chip FTSE 100 index and in some 60 others.

"This is a huge landmark in the development of our UK equity activities," Smith said. "We have always seen it as very important to offer a whole equity service and it is nice to add another part of the jigsaw."
The start of trading in UK equities comes two months after Smith started at DMG after joining from rival brokerage UBS, where he was head of European research.

Deutsche first set out its aim of rebuilding a presence in European equities in 1995, based on its Morgan Grenfell arm acquired in 1990. A huge 300,000 sq ft headquarters for the investment bank is under construction in London's financial district.

Morgan Grenfell had pulled out of equities in the wake of the stock market crash of 1987 but Deutsche decided it needed to re-establish a presence in trading and researching stocks to complement other areas of its business.

The past year has seen the firm embark on a costly and high-profile hiring exercise aimed at luring equity analysts, traders and sales staff from rivals but the house has denied rivals' allegations of overpaying to attract top individuals.
Smith said DMG had last week hired equity salesmen Rick Saunders and Peter Wiley from U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley, joining the near 80 equity recruits it has made over the past year.
Yet he said a round of hirings of specific UK equity staff, as opposed to the pan-European staff so far taken on, had yet to begin in earnest.
Smith said the start of equity market-making, signalled by the appearance of the initials DMG on London Stock Exchange dealing screens at the start of trading today, had been deliberately low-key.
"All we have tried to do is ease ourselves into the business," he said.

Market-making was seen as part of an integrated equity service to the bank's clients but was intended to be profitable, he added. "We are not in the business to lose money, I think clients expect that and respect us for it."
